source.title: Scaling antibody language models improves structure aware representation for antibody engineering
source.authors: Sheng-Yuan Bai; Zi-Jing Liu; Bing Feng; Ji-Ying Zhang; Yu Li

record.file_problem: Full article-in-press text is present. It is described as an unedited manuscript and has minor text-extraction spacing artifacts; it is not cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study directly tests whether antibody sequence models show scaling behavior, using evaluation perplexity across model sizes and pretraining data volumes. This is a different biological sequence setting and does not test compute-optimal allocation.
record.gate_note: Figure 1G and the text report evaluation perplexity scaling. Downstream task comparisons and training-data ablations are not rows for the stated scaling versions: they do not report how downstream performance tracks pretraining loss or model scale as claimed in V6.
record.test_reason: The paper reports eval perplexity for 300M, 600M and 1.7B antibody BERT models and states it falls as a power law with model size and data volume. This is a new setting (antibody sequences, masked LM) with a result on the power-law form, so it bears on V1 and V5. It gives no fitted exponents, no extrapolation test, and no compute-optimal analysis.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct: the authors say perplexity falls with model size and pretraining data following a power law and call this predictable scaling. The record should note that they give no fitted coefficients and do not separate size from data effects.
record.recipe_differences: Uses antibody-specific BERT models with TripleAA tokenization and CRT, reports evaluation perplexity, and scales parameter count and pretraining data together. It does not report compute-optimal allocation or numeric fitted exponents.
record.method_sensitivity: The analysis varies model size and pretraining data volume together: the 300M and 600M models use 300M sequences, while the 1.7B model uses 1.4 billion sequences. Evaluation perplexity is also shown over training steps.
record.problems: Scaling results are shown in a figure without numerical perplexity values or reported fitted coefficients in the text. Model size and data volume are not independently varied, and the tested ranges are limited relative to the claim's several-orders-of-magnitude scope.
record.rows_left_out: No additional scaling-related results on the stated versions were reported separately. Downstream-task and training-data-size results were not extracted because they do not measure the claimed relationship between pretraining loss and scale.

untested.parts: Text-pretraining power law over several orders of magnitude, with size, data or compute isolated; this study covers antibody sequences only.
Image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer as scaling-law settings. Downstream gains are shown but not tied to a scaling law.
No extrapolation from small fits to larger runs.
No architecture shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Downstream results are not plotted against pretraining loss or scale in a way that tests V6, apart from some training-data ablations on downstream tasks.
No comparison of fitting choices or exponents.

missing.what: Fitted power-law coefficients and numeric perplexity values for each model
missing.locator: Figure 1G; Results 2.1 mention 'corresponding scaling coefficients' that are not reported

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 link and V1 'supports' label are not warranted. Three sizes, with data changing alongside size, in a narrow range do not test the several-orders-of-magnitude power-law claim for text pretraining. The record's V5 'supports' is also too strong, hence limits_scope. The claim of being the 'pioneering' model to show scaling is the authors' own.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports evaluation perplexity, not cross-entropy values; does not isolate parameter count from pretraining data volume; and does not establish behavior over several orders of magnitude or test compute scaling.
Tests antibody sequence models only; does not test image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer as settings for a scaling law.

rows.subject: AbLingua-300M
rows.operation_detail: Evaluation perplexity was plotted during pretraining as a function of training step in the model-size and data-volume scaling analysis.

conditions.value: Figure 1G plots evaluation perplexity over steps; x-axis extends to 200 (1k)

rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation across five independent runs are reported for performance metrics; model-specific values are not stated here.
rows.note: The authors state that perplexity decreases as model parameter count and pretraining data volume increase, following a power-law relationship. The plotted value for this model is not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: Figure-only, no numbers. Model size and data volume are confounded, and the form is asserted rather than shown by a fit. Three model sizes in a 300M-1.7B range cannot support a power-law fit over several orders of magnitude, so it should not bear on V1. 'Observed' is too strong; the text says only that perplexity falls.

rows.subject: AbLingua-600M
rows.operation_detail: Evaluation perplexity was plotted during pretraining as a function of training step in the model-size and data-volume scaling analysis.

conditions.value: Figure 1G plots evaluation perplexity over steps; x-axis extends to 200 (1k)

rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation across five independent runs are reported for performance metrics; model-specific values are not stated here.
rows.note: The authors state that perplexity decreases as model parameter count and pretraining data volume increase, following a power-law relationship. The plotted value for this model is not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: Same as R1. The 600M model shares its 300M-sequence data with the 300M model, so these two differ only in size. Power-law form is asserted, not shown. Not a V1 row.

rows.subject: AbLingua-1.7B
rows.operation_detail: Evaluation perplexity was plotted during pretraining as a function of training step in the model-size and data-volume scaling analysis.

conditions.value: Figure 1G plots evaluation perplexity over steps; x-axis extends to 200 (1k)

rows.uncertainty: Mean and standard deviation across five independent runs are reported for performance metrics; model-specific values are not stated here.
rows.note: The authors state that perplexity decreases as model parameter count and pretraining data volume increase, following a power-law relationship. The plotted value for this model is not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: The 1.7B model changes both size and data (1.4B sequences) relative to R1 and R2, so this is a confounded point. Values are not tabulated. Not a V1 row. The 1.7B curve is also not clearly lower on its own; only the authors' statement supports it.

relationships.condition: Antibody BERT models, 300M-1.7B parameters, size and data scaled together, 3 points
relationships.reason: Authors claim power-law decrease in eval perplexity (R1-R3), but there are only three confounded points, no fitted exponents or numbers, and a masked-LM objective, so the form is asserted rather than demonstrated.
relationships.display_finding: Joint increases in model size and data lowered evaluation perplexity across three points, leaving the claimed power-law form unquantified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: AbLingua antibody sequence models in the reported parameter/data scaling sweep
reader_labels.reason: The authors state that evaluation perplexity decreases with increasing parameter count and pretraining data volume and follows a power-law relationship (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The tested parameter range is 300M–1.7B and data volume changes alongside model size; the study does not isolate either variable or show several orders of magnitude (R1–R3).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study reports power-law-like evaluation-perplexity scaling for antibody-specific sequence models, extending the analysis to this biological sequence setting (R1–R3).
